title: Rhymes, Chants and Story Responses
introduction: Enjoy rhythm and respond to characters, actions and settings in short texts.
definition: Enjoy rhythm and respond to characters, actions and settings in short texts.
rules: Say rhyming lines aloud and listen to their rhythm.
Name characters and settings, and create short original lines with a partner.

examples.question: Complete the rhyme: I see a bright light, shining in the ___. (night or day)
steps: Light and night have matching ending sounds.

examples.question: Which rhymes with boat: coat or book?
steps: Boat and coat share the same final sound.

exercises.question: Complete the rhyme: I see a bright light, shining in the ___. (night or day)
exercises.solution: Light and night have matching ending sounds.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with boat: coat or book?
exercises.solution: Boat and coat share the same final sound.

exercises.question: Read: A small robot waves to Mei. Name the person.
exercises.solution: Mei is the named person in the line.

exercises.question: Read: A crab hides in the sand. Where is it hiding?
exercises.solution: The phrase after hides gives the setting.

exercises.question: Complete the chant: Clap your hands, tap your ___. (feet or hat)
exercises.solution: Tapping your feet is an action that fits the chant.

exercises.question: Which rhymes with play: day or dog?
exercises.solution: Play and day share the long a ending sound.

summary: Enjoy rhythm and respond to characters, actions and settings in short texts. Say rhyming lines aloud and listen to their rhythm.
